# HTG equilibrium case file.
#
# Run it with:      uv run htg run my_case.toml
# Check it first:   uv run htg check my_case.toml     (fast; no equation of state)
# Species names:    uv run htg species --search methane
#
# Units: temperature in °C, pressure in bar (absolute). Species amounts
# (constraints, results) are mol per mol of carbon in the dry feed. Carbon
# shares are fractions (0.9 = 90 %).
# Lines starting with # are comments. Delete or comment out what you don't need;
# anything left out takes its default value.

format = 2
name = "my_case"
description = "What this case is about."

# Optional atomic-weight overrides [g/mol]. They change the feed and balance
# arithmetic only (not the equation-of-state molar masses).
# atomic_weights = { C = 12.011, H = 1.008 }

[conditions]
temperature_C = [300, 350, 400, 450]   # one value, or a list for a sweep
pressure_bar = 240.0                   # one value, or a list: every temperature at every pressure
# Instead of the two lines above, explicit (temperature, pressure) points, solved in this order:
# points = [[300, 240], [350, 250], [400, 260]]

[feed]
# The wet feed going into the reactor: solids plus water.
total_kg = 5.0                              # solids + water
solids = { value = 20.0, unit = "%" }       # "%" of the total mass, or "kg"
ash = { value = 8.44, unit = "%" }          # "%" of the solids, or "kg"; leave out for no ash
# Elemental analysis, mass % of the ash-free solids, as entered. Scaled to sum
# to 100 % when used.
elements_wt_percent = { C = 30.4, H = 4.41, O = 53.58, N = 2.66, S = 0.51 }
# Or, instead of the four lines above, amounts of species (no ash in this mode):
# [feed.species]
# water = { value = 4.5, unit = "kg" }      # always present; "kg" or "mol"
# cellulose = { value = 0.5, unit = "kg" }

# Added salts supply atoms only; the products decide where those atoms go.
# Every salt element needs a product that can carry it (an ion or a mineral).
# [feed.salts.NaHCO3]
# mol_per_g_dry_feed = 1e-5
# elements = { Na = 1, H = 1, C = 1, O = 3 }

[phases]
# The products allowed in each phase. A species in a list may form; it is not forced.
# Ions (e.g. "Na+") are allowed in the aqueous phase only.
gas = ["water", "hydrogen", "carbon dioxide", "carbon monoxide", "methane",
       "methanol", "ammonia", "hydrogen sulfide", "nitrogen", "unobtainium"]
aqueous = ["water", "hydrogen", "carbon dioxide", "carbon monoxide", "methane",
           "methanol", "ammonia", "hydrogen sulfide"]
organic_liquid = ["benzene", "toluene"]
solid = ["carbon"]

[aqueous]
model = "electrolyte"     # "electrolyte" (ePC-SAFT, ions allowed) or "molecular" (PC-SAFT)
cutoff_C = 390.0          # no aqueous phase at and above this temperature (a modelling rule)
# enabled = false         # no aqueous phase at any temperature
# water_floor = 1e-8      # minimum aqueous water, mol/mol C

[constraints]
# solid_carbon_target = "char"       # what "solid" means below: "char" (solid carbon only) or "all_solids"
# [constraints.minimum_amounts]      # lower bounds, mol/mol C
# gas = { water = 1e-8 }

# Share of the feed carbon in each phase, as fractions of all feed carbon.
# Per phase: exact, or min and/or max. A phase left out is free.
# [constraints.carbon]
# gas = { min = 0.9 }
# solid = { max = 0.05 }
# aqueous = { exact = 0.03 }         # dropped at temperatures without an aqueous phase

[solver]
method = "ipopt"          # "ipopt" (default), "slsqp", "trust-constr", or "slsqp-fd" (original)
# starts = 5              # starting points in total; distinct results are all kept
# distinct_composition_tol = 1e-4   # results differ if any amount differs by more [mol/mol C]
# distinct_gibbs_tol = 1.0          # ... or if the Gibbs energies differ by more [J/mol C]
# max_iterations = 5000

[initial_guess]
initialization = "auto"   # "auto", "liquid" (water-rich aqueous), "vapor" (water-rich gas), "lp"

[sweep]
# Start each point from the previous solution: along rising temperature at each
# pressure, or in the order of the points list. false: every point starts fresh
# (then all points can run in parallel).
continuation = true

# Data to show next to the results in plots (CSV: T_C column, then "phase:species" columns).

# file = "comparison/my_data.csv"
# quantity = "mol_per_kg_dry_feed"   # or "mol_per_mol_C", "g_per_kg_dry_feed"

# Swine manure, reproducing Yakaboylu et al. (2013), Figures 7 and 8.
# Reduced C/H/O/N/S feed (atom inventory per 25 000 g dry manure), char as the
# only solid, nitrogen in the gas only, aqueous phase removed at and above 390 °C.
# Carbon allocation is free.

format = 2
name = "cli_run_small"
description = "Swine manure at 240 bar; Yakaboylu et al. (2013) Figures 7-8."

[conditions]
temperature_C = [300, 389.6, 450]
pressure_bar = 240.0

[feed]
# C 632.65, H 1093.28, O 837.22, N 47.56, S 3.95 mol and 5550.84 mol water per
# 25 000 g dry feed. The 8.45 % of the dry feed outside these elements is ash.
total_kg = 4.999935304
solids = { value = 1.0, unit = "kg" }
ash = { value = 8.44688764, unit = "%" }
elements_wt_percent = { C = 30.3950366, H = 4.40810496, O = 53.57873112, N = 2.66469168, S = 0.506548 }

[phases]
gas = ["water", "hydrogen", "carbon dioxide", "carbon monoxide", "methane",
       "methanol", "ammonia", "hydrogen sulfide", "nitrogen"]
# Note from the original notebook: with nitrogen also in the aqueous phase,
# the solver converges to a different solution at 380 °C.
aqueous = ["water", "hydrogen", "carbon dioxide", "carbon monoxide", "methane",
           "methanol", "ammonia", "hydrogen sulfide"]
organic_liquid = ["benzene", "toluene"]
solid = ["carbon"]

[aqueous]
model = "electrolyte"
cutoff_C = 390.0

[initial_guess]
# Water-rich aqueous start below the cut-off; a plain feasible start above it.
initialization = "liquid"

[solver]
method = "ipopt"
max_iterations = 10000
# The original notebook used method = "slsqp-fd" with these settings:
fd_ftol = 1e-11
fd_eps = 1e-8

[sweep]
continuation = false   # every temperature starts from its own feasible point, as in the notebook

[comparison]
file = "comparison/yakaboylu2013_fig7_8.csv"
quantity = "mol_per_kg_dry_feed"
label = "Yakaboylu et al. (2013)"
